summary: Moosehead Mountain lookout (St. Lawrence County, 1910), taken down in 1978 and re-erected in 2016 in a Brooklyn courtyard at Industry City; not climbable since at least 2021.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-25 steel tower, 40 feet, with external ladder access (erected 1916 at Moosehead Mountain)

access.note: Stands in a courtyard on the Industry City campus, which the contractor describes as having three public courtyards; no later access rule found

events.note: State fire superintendents decided to add a lookout at Moosehead Mountain to the existing observation stations (October 7, 1909)
A lookout was established atop a 20-foot tower at Moosehead Mountain, cost $442.26
W.D. Pond of Childwood appointed forest observer for Moosehead Mountain for the fire season
A 40-foot Aermotor LS-25 steel tower with external ladder access was erected; the source does not say whether it replaced the 1910 tower
April 1950 newspaper said Mrs. Pearl Eakins of Conifer would again be observer, the only woman observer in Northern New York
Dismantled by a private party and stored for later re-assembly at Moosehead Mountain
Refurbished by Dave Vana of Davana LLC before re-erection
Re-erected in Brooklyn in a courtyard at Industry City in October 2016

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's relocation has no year; the 2016 chapter report and November 2016 newsletter both date the re-erection in Brooklyn to October 2016

notes_for_editor: Correction proposed, not applied: county Suffolk should read Kings (Brooklyn). Height is unresolved: the 1910 lookout was a 20-foot tower and the 1916 erection was a 40-foot Aermotor LS-25, and the source does not say whether the second replaced the first. The sibling record us-ny-moosehead-mountain has height_m 6.1 (20 feet) and may describe only the 1910 tower; left unchanged. The record's 'rebuilt' 2016 event is kept in the record but the sources say refurbished and re-erected. Access and climbability rest on a May 2021 visitor blog; nothing later was found, and the Todd Group page is a contractor's marketing page. Historical facts come from the Forest Lookouts compilation of newspaper items, not the originals. Used 1 WebSearch and 4 page reads plus one cached local page.
